surfaceForm: \institution{RESTENA} (Luxembourg). The Luxembourg NREN connects the country's research and education community to GÉANT and operates institutional services under the RESTENA-CSIRT umbrella. RESTENA's role as a shared operator is relevant to several of the architecture's mutualisation patterns.
location: ch31-institutional-precedents-EN.tex / Section: NRENs and consortium initiatives (sec:ip-nrens)
proposedGenericDecision: Within the NREN catalogue, RESTENA may remain as ONE entry among peer NRENs (DFN, SWITCH, RENATER, JISC/Janet, Internet2, RNP, AARNet) since the chapter is a multi-region catalogue. But the framing 'RESTENA's role as a shared operator is relevant to several of the architecture's mutualisation patterns' singles out the home NREN as the reference operator for THIS architecture. Generalise to: 'the adopting institution's national NREN is the relevant shared operator for the mutualisation patterns', with RESTENA demoted to a same-weight catalogue entry.
rationale: RESTENA is the University of Luxembourg's actual national NREN. The sentence binding RESTENA specifically to 'the architecture's mutualisation patterns' is the home-institution leak; the catalogue listing itself is legitimate precedent material. Note RESTENA-CSIRT is the home CSIRT umbrella.

surfaceForm: \gls{restena} in Luxembourg~\cite{restena}, DFN in Germany~\cite{dfn} and SWITCH in Switzerland~\cite{switch-nren} are mandated accordingly.
location: ch31-institutional-precedents-EN.tex / Section: The precedents illustrate the architecture; they do not gate it (sec:ip-beyond-flagship), paragraph 'The shared-service channel'
proposedGenericDecision: The list of three NRENs to illustrate the shared-service mandate is fine as a multi-country example, but RESTENA/Luxembourg is consistently placed first as the lead exemplar, which reflects home-institution authorship. Reorder/neutralise so no single NREN is the lead, or parameterize the lead example to the adopter's own NREN ('e.g., \HOME_NREN in \HOME_COUNTRY, alongside DFN in Germany and SWITCH in Switzerland').
rationale: RESTENA-in-Luxembourg-first ordering is a tell of the home jurisdiction. The trio as illustration of NREN mandates is otherwise generic and citable; only the lead-position bias needs neutralising.

surfaceForm: the international university network anticipated in phase~2 of this initiative ... The phase-2 international network is the natural locus for this refresh. ... The phase-2 international network (\S\ref{sec:ip-method}) is the natural locus for recording such adoptions ... The phase-2 international university network is the locus where these gaps would be addressed
location: ch31-institutional-precedents-EN.tex / Sections: chapter intro, Method (Refresh cadence), sec:ip-beyond-flagship (Implication for the catalogue), Documented gaps (sec:ip-gaps)
proposedGenericDecision: 'phase 2 of this initiative' and 'the phase-2 international university network' name a specific roadmap of the originating (UL) project. A reusable Reference cannot assume the adopter runs the same two-phase initiative or the same network. Generalise to a role-based construct: 'a community of practice / adopting-institution network maintaining this catalogue', dropping the phase-2 / initiative chronology.
rationale: 'phase 2 of this initiative' is a project-lifecycle reference specific to the source programme; it appears four times as the maintenance/refresh locus and presumes the reader is inside the same initiative. The underlying idea (a shared catalogue maintained collaboratively) is generic; the phase-2/initiative branding is not.

surfaceForm: this Reference (recurring, e.g. 'The architecture and playbook of this Reference', 'feeding this Reference', 'novel to this Reference', "this Reference's federated-governance discussions", "this Reference's discussion of compute")
location: ch31-institutional-precedents-EN.tex / throughout (chapter intro; sec:ip-europe ETH paragraph; sec:ip-north-america Indiana; sec:ip-gaps)
proposedGenericDecision: 'this Reference' is the document's own self-name; it is institution-agnostic in itself but is the suite-internal product label. Keep if the suite standardises on 'this Reference' as the generic document self-name; confirm it is not an alias for a UL-branded title elsewhere.
rationale: Self-reference is not a jurisdictional/institutional leak per se. Flagged only for consistency review: if elsewhere the suite gives 'this Reference' a UL-specific proper title, that title is the leak, not these in-text uses.

surfaceForm: operates institutional services under the RESTENA-CSIRT umbrella
location: ch31-institutional-precedents-EN.tex / Section: NRENs and consortium initiatives (sec:ip-nrens), RESTENA paragraph
proposedGenericDecision: RESTENA-CSIRT is the home incident-response umbrella. As a factual catalogue detail about RESTENA it is acceptable precedent content; but it should not be presented as THE CSIRT umbrella for the adopting institution. Keep as a descriptive fact within the RESTENA entry only.
rationale: Descriptive of RESTENA itself (legitimate catalogue fact), but named because RESTENA-CSIRT is the actual home-country CSIRT and could be mistaken for a generic recommendation. Parameterize only if reused outside the RESTENA entry.

surfaceForm: CERN, ETH Zürich, University of Cambridge, University of Oxford, KU Leuven, MIT, Stanford University, University of Michigan, Indiana University, University of Toronto, National University of Singapore, Australian National University, Tsinghua University, Universidade de São Paulo, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, GÉANT, Internet2, JISC, RNP, AARNet, DFN, SWITCH
location: ch31-institutional-precedents-EN.tex / Sections: European/North American/Asia-Pacific/Latin American institutions; NRENs and consortium initiatives
proposedGenericDecision: These are EXTERNAL precedent institutions and are the legitimate subject matter of an 'Institutional precedents' catalogue. They do not bind the document to a home institution. Keep wholesale; do not generalise.
rationale: The chapter's purpose is to catalogue named external institutions as illustrative precedents. Genericising these would destroy the chapter. Listed here explicitly to document the DETECTION decision that they are intentional, not leaks. RESTENA is the one exception handled in its own rows above.

surfaceForm: A national research-and-education network exists to serve its country's entire research and education community, not its flagship institutions alone ... an institution that consumes federated identity through its NREN ... at a realisation it can sustain.
location: ch31-institutional-precedents-EN.tex / Section: sec:ip-beyond-flagship, paragraph 'The shared-service channel'
proposedGenericDecision: This passage is already written generically ('its country', 'its NREN') — good model for the rest of the chapter. No change needed; flagged as the template the RESTENA-specific sentences should be aligned to.
rationale: Positive control: demonstrates the role-based phrasing the document should use everywhere. Included so the generalisation of the RESTENA rows has a same-document style anchor.

surfaceForm: \trchap{ch:architectural-principles}{} (\S\ref{sec:ap-necessity}) ... \trchap{ch:wave1-identity}{} ... the minimal necessary set for any institution offering a digital infrastructure
proposedGenericDecision: Internal cross-references to sibling chapters of the same Reference. Institution-agnostic provided those target chapters are themselves generalised. Keep; track as dependency for suite-wide consistency rather than a standalone leak.
rationale: Cross-refs to ch:architectural-principles and ch:wave1-identity are suite-internal and carry the 'minimal necessary set' framing, which is the project's size-invariant defense — generic by design. No home-institution binding here; noted only for traceability.
